slides.0.title: Cornas, Saint-Péray and the northern Rhône fringes
slides.0.subtitle: 100% Syrah, whites and sparkling
slides.1.title: Cornas: 100% Syrah red
slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOC and area
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Recognised by decree on 5 August 1938; the area is the single commune of Cornas in the Ardèche; still red only. About 162 ha in 2025 (Inter Rhône)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Syrah only
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The specification says the wines come from Syrah; its tasting section notes that Cornas is the only northern appellation made exclusively from Syrah (Côte-Rôtie and Hermitage allow other grapes)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Yield and alcohol
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Yield 40 hl/ha (ceiling 46; above 50 the whole harvest loses the AOC); minimum natural alcohol 10.5%
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Terrain and soil (common view)
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Sun-facing amphitheatre slopes, commonly said to be well sheltered from wind; granite (called gore in CMS materials). The name is often glossed "burnt earth" — common wisdom, not tested
slides.1.content: Memory hooks for Cornas: right bank, Ardèche, a single commune, 100% Syrah, red only.
slides.2.title: Saint-Péray: from sparkling to still white
slides.2.highlights.0.title: AOC and location
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Granted AOC status on 8 December 1936 (its 90th anniversary is 2026); in the Ardèche opposite Valence, with the Crussol limestone massif as its landmark, plus granite, alluvium and loess
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Marsanne and Roussanne
slides.2.highlights.1.content: White grapes only: Marsanne and Roussanne, varietal or blended in any ratio; roughly three quarters Marsanne and one quarter Roussanne (Drive notes)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Styles: still and sparkling
slides.2.highlights.2.content: White only, both still and sparkling; sparkling is about 5–10% of volume depending on the year. Champagne-method sparkling appeared from about 1829, and the 19th century was its sparkling golden age
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Decline and revival
slides.2.highlights.3.content: In 1936 about 250–300 ha, 90% for sparkling; urban growth left only about 45 ha by 1990; today still whites drive the revival. Area: 116 ha in the Drive notes, 128 ha in Inter Rhône 2025 (sources differ, not tested)
slides.2.content: Saint-Péray is a white-only AOC: still wine is the mainstay, sparkling its historic calling card.
slides.3.title: Northern fringes: Brézème, Seyssuel and the Diois
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Brézème
slides.3.highlights.0.content: At Livron-sur-Drôme on left-bank slopes, the southernmost tip of the northern Rhône bordering the south. It is not a stand-alone AOC but part of the regional Côtes du Rhône; 11 estates run joint marketing (Drive notes)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Seyssuel
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Replanted slopes near Vienne at the far north; commonly placed in the IGP Collines Rhodaniennes (the IGP specification was not checked line by line, so not tested). Domaine Verzier and others have invested here recently
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The Montélimar parallel
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The 30% Grenache minimum of Côtes du Rhône is waived for estates north of the Montélimar parallel (Drôme), reflecting the Syrah-led north
slides.3.highlights.3.title: The Diois (next lesson)
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Clairette de Die and Crémant de Die in the Drôme foothills are south-eastern France's sparkling zone, covered in the next lesson with the outlying names
slides.3.content: Fringe names are mostly not stand-alone AOCs; always check their legal status first.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What are the permitted grape and wine type of Cornas?
B. Mostly Syrah with Viognier allowed, red
Cornas makes still red wine from Syrah alone.
B. White (still and sparkling) from Marsanne and Roussanne
Saint-Péray makes only white, still and sparkling, from Marsanne and Roussanne.
What is the legal status of Brézème?
B. Part of the regional Côtes du Rhône appellation
Brézème is not a stand-alone AOC; it belongs to Côtes du Rhône (Drive notes of Bourgogne Aujourd'hui).
On which bank and in which département is Cornas?
Cornas is a single commune in the Ardèche on the right bank.
